title: Raghuram Rajan, Raj Chetty, Asha Sharma Named to Lead Key Fed Monetary Policy Task Forces
excerpt: Former RBI Governor Rajan will co-lead the Balance Sheet Policy panel, while Harvard's Chetty and Microsoft Xbox chief Sharma head data and productivity teams under Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's reform push.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Three Indian-origin leaders named to co-chair Federal Reserve task forces examining monetary policy reform
  • Raghuram Rajan will review the Fed's balance sheet regime alongside Karen Dynan and Jeremy Stein
  • Raj Chetty leads the data task force; Asha Sharma joins the productivity and jobs panel alongside Marc Andreessen

Three Indian-origin leaders have been named to co-chair Federal Reserve task forces as part of a sweeping review of the central bank's monetary policy framework, underscoring the growing influence of Indian-American expertise at the highest levels of U.S. economic policymaking.

Rajan Returns to the Fed Orbit

Fed Chair Kevin Warsh announced the leadership lineup for five new task forces designed to examine and modernize the central bank's operations. Former Reserve Bank of India Governor Raghuram Rajan has been named to co-lead the Balance Sheet Policy task force, which will "examine the costs, benefits, and institutional implications" of the Fed's balance sheet regime.

Rajan, who currently serves as the Katherine Dusak Miller Distinguished Service Professor of Finance at the University of Chicago Booth School of Business, is widely known for warning global central bankers at Jackson Hole in 2005 about banks' growing subprime loan books — a warning that preceded the 2008 global financial crisis. He becomes the first former RBI governor to join a U.S. Fed special team.

He will work alongside Harvard economist and former Treasury official Karen Dynan and former Fed Governor Jeremy Stein on the balance sheet panel.

Chetty on Data, Sharma on AI and Jobs

Harvard economist Raj Chetty, known for using large datasets to study economic mobility, will co-chair the Data task force alongside former Walmart CEO Doug McMillon and University of Chicago economist Kevin Murphy. The panel will focus on finding faster and more accurate ways to read real-world economic signals.

Asha Sharma, executive vice president and Xbox CEO at Microsoft, will co-lead the Productivity and Jobs task force. Her co-chairs include venture capitalist Marc Andreessen and Stanford economist Charles I. Jones. The panel will study how emerging technologies — particularly artificial intelligence — are reshaping the workplace and affecting business growth.

A Broader Reform Push

"The goal is straightforward: to ensure the Fed is best positioned to achieve our objectives in this consequential time," Warsh said while announcing the lineup, which draws on academics, former central bankers, and corporate executives.

The five task forces will work independently to review the Fed's tools and strategies, with recommendations expected to shape the central bank's approach during a period of post-inflation economic recalibration. The panels bring together economists, business leaders, and former central bank officials to review everything from monetary policy communications to the impact of AI on employment.

What It Means for the Diaspora

The appointments reflect a broader pattern of Indian-origin professionals reaching pivotal roles in U.S. economic governance. Any policy shifts emerging from these task forces — particularly on interest rates, the Fed's balance sheet, and AI-driven labor market changes — could have direct implications for Indian-American homeowners, tech workers, and investors watching the Fed's next moves.
